title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 48-52): Grothendieck is setting up level-2 / octahedral structures on P^1-bundles X/S (residue characteristics ≠ 2). This is meant for moduli of elliptic curves, using the line E/{±1} with the action of E[2] by translations.

Definition. Let Δ ⊂ X be a finite étale divisor of degree 6 over S. An octahedral structure on Δ is a fixed-point-free involution σ_Δ : Δ → Δ (an 'antipodism'), i.e. a free action of Z/2 on Δ/S. Δ is then split into three antipodal pairs, the three 'axes'. Earlier drafts (crossed out) phrased this via a quotient Δ' finite étale of degree 3.

Groups. Aut_oct(Δ) is the centralizer of σ_Δ, étale-locally the hyperoctahedral group (Z/2)^3 ⋊ S_3 of order 48. Aut^+_oct(Δ) is the index-2 subgroup of 'direct' automorphisms, locally ≅ S_4, the rotation group of the octahedron.

Regularity. The structure is called regular relative to X if Γ = Aut^+_oct(Δ) acts on X compatibly with its action on Δ. Such an action is then unique, because by p.49 an automorphism of P^1 fixing pointwise a 2-element subset of Δ other than an axis is trivial.

Claims on the page:
(1) Given an action of Γ on X and the divisor Δ, there is at most one regular octahedral structure on Δ.
(2) Such a structure exists iff Δ is an 'octahedral configuration', i.e. an orbit of type {0,∞,±1,±i}. By p.49 such a configuration carries a canonical octahedral structure, and the S_4 it determines makes it regular.
(3) Conversely, from a regular structure one gets the minimal nontrivial normal subgroup V ⊂ Γ. V is locally isomorphic to the Klein group (written D_2, on the next page (D_4)_S), it acts on X, and the configuration is recovered as the union of the fixed-point divisors of the three involutions of V.

This prepares the theorem on p.51: canonical compatible bijections between
- Klein-four subgroup schemes V ⊂ Aut_S(X) = PGL(1)-form,
- S_4 subgroup schemes Γ ⊂ Aut_S(X),
- regular octahedral configurations in X.

Marginal remarks:
- A digression on the fixed divisors of the involutions in P^1_S.
- If Δ is a regular octahedral configuration in X, the double cover of orientations of Δ (the torsor of the quotient Aut_oct/Aut^+_oct = Z/2) is canonically isomorphic to μ_4^* = Spec O_S[i]/(i^2+1), the scheme of primitive 4th roots of unity. Concretely, an orientation picks out the quarter-turn about each axis in the positive sense. Its multiplier (derivative) at the 'positive' pole is a primitive 4th root of unity: z ↦ iz at 0 versus z ↦ -iz.
errors: Notation is inconsistent for the Klein four group: 'D_2' (written D_{2S}) here versus '(D_4)_S' on p.51. Both mean the dihedral group of order 4, (Z/2)^2. This is a notational slip, not a mathematical error.
On the next page the configurations are called 'icosaédrales'. This is a slip for 'octaédrales' (the same slip was already corrected once on p.51).

The sentence 'on vient de voir qu'elle est munie d'une structure octaédrale…' relies on p.49. There uniqueness of the structure was checked only on the standard model {0,∞,±1,±i}, extended 'par raison d'homogénéité'. Over a general base S this needs étale-local reduction to the standard model, which is implicit but fine.

ideas.what: Octahedral structure on a degree-6 étale divisor as a free involution; Aut^+_oct ≅ S_4 inside the hyperoctahedral group of order 48
ideas.modern_name: octahedral group / hyperoctahedral group B_3 acting on antipodal 6-point configuration

ideas.what: Bijection between Klein-four subgroups, S_4 subgroups of a PGL_2-form, and regular octahedral 6-point configurations, relative over a base S with 2 invertible
ideas.modern_name: finite subgroups of PGL_2 over a base / forms of finite subgroup schemes; relative Klein classification
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical over C (Klein); relative versions folklore (e.g. Beauville, Serre on finite subgroups of PGL_2)

ideas.what: Orientation double cover of a regular octahedral configuration canonically ≅ μ_4^* (primitive 4th roots of unity) via the multiplier of the positive quarter-turn at its fixed pole
ideas.modern_name: rotation-number / multiplier character; Galois descent identifying the orientation torsor with Spec Z[1/2][i]-torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (implicit in descent of octahedral forms of P^1)

ideas.what: Klein four subgroup V of Aut(P^1) as the image of E[2] acting on E/{±1}, used toward modular curves in char ≠ 2
ideas.modern_name: level-2 structure via the 2-torsion action on the x-line (Legendre/Kummer)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Klein); in moduli form Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur

missed.claim: A canonical identification of the orientation Z/2-torsor of a regular octahedral configuration over any base S (2 invertible) with the torsor μ_4^* of primitive 4th roots of unity. This means the 'orientation' obstruction for descending S_4 ⊂ PGL_2-forms is exactly the Galois action on i. It is a neat, scheme-theoretic formulation, but almost certainly known in substance.
missed.quote: le revêtement double des orientations de Δ est canoniquement isomorphe au revêtement μ_4^* Spec O_S[i]/(i^2+1) de S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a clean relative statement of why octahedral (S_4) forms of P^1 over a base split into two classes governed by Q(i), which is relevant to arithmetic of S_4-covers and level structures. It is marginal novelty only.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful relative (over a base S) reformulation of Klein's classical classification of octahedral subgroups of PGL_2, tied to level-2 structure of elliptic curves. It is correct and elegant but essentially classical. The μ_4^* orientation remark is a nice canonical detail, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'invariant [?] ... trivial [?]' likely reads 'invariant minimal non trivial' (or similar): V is the minimal nontrivial normal subgroup of Γ ≅ S_4.
'groupe loc. isom. à 𝔻_{2S}' is the Klein four group (Z/2)^2, written D_2. On p.51 it is written (D_4)_S, with the subscript indicating order 4.
In the first margin note, '𝒢_Δ' is probably σ_Δ or 'Γ_Δ'. The note concerns the fixed points of the involutions in P^1_S.
'(x.?)' at top right is probably a section label such as '(x.2)' or a page cross-reference, not mathematics.
